AboutMeIntro.heading: Olá 👋
AboutMeIntro.subheading: I believe in the power of design to solve complex social problems.

profile_pic.alt: Incredibly photogenic picture of me looking straight into the camera.

AboutMeDescription.text: What's so great about design is that it is a process. It forces you to position yourself in the users' shoes and think like them, to live their struggle. Only then is it possible to understand the solution to be built. I think people focus too much on what a tool does and not so much on the problem it solves, the purpose it serves. I build good tools because I focus on this aspect and never forget about it, and decisions come naturally this way. My talent is combining design and technology to build things people like to use.

InfrastructureIntro.heading: How to design cities
InfrastructureIntro.paragraph_1: The Dutch are very practical when it comes to designing their cities.
InfrastructureIntro.paragraph_2: It is a misconception that the Netherlands has great bike usage because it is flat—it is because it has great infrastructure. Cities around the world must learn from the best, starting with these three examples of thoughtful design and engineering, and integration of the various components that make a city.
InfrastructureIntro.paragraph_3: Roads are the arteries of the city, and the Netherlands' have never been healthier.
InfrastructureIntro.paragraph_4: Take a look at BicycleDutch on his <anchor_1>blog</anchor_1> and on <anchor_2>YouTube</anchor_2>.

WorkIntro.heading: It is very easy to be different, but very difficult to be better.
WorkIntro.paragraph: Building better tools is what wakes me up in the morning. It all starts by defining the problem to be solved and thinking about it from the user's perspective. Only by focusing hard on this approach is it possible to be confident in one's decisions. The following examples combine design, technology, and a lot of dedication to create intuitive tools that simplify its users' lives.
